comparator.name: Natural Sciences
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 formally adopted Faculty of Science EER; current 180-EC standard route
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 EER, Arts. 7.3–7.5, defines 60 EC first-year compulsory physics, mathematics, chemistry and biochemistry; 30 EC later shared compulsory courses; a 72-EC formal specialisation; 6 EC free electives; and a 12-EC Bachelor’s Internship and Report as individual final project. For the first-listed Physical Chemistry specialisation, 33 EC of named courses are required and 39 EC is restricted choice from eligible non-overlapping Faculty of Science bachelor courses and/or a permitted minor. Total: 60+30+33+39+6+12=180. The other two specialisations, Biophysics and Biochemistry, are mutually exclusive and are not mixed into this route. First-listed instances are used only for alternative course groups within the selected route; they are not UCR-matching selections. The 0-EC first-year Academic Skills subcomponent and RADAr assessment carry no additional credits. Prospective 2027–28 programme pages illustrate routes but the adopted 2026–27 EER controls requirements. The programme language is Dutch though most courses are taught in English.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The first programme integrates life science with evolution, Earth systems, climate, sustainability and a broad mathematics line. The second concentrates on molecular, cellular and biomedical biology, replacing eleven environmental, Earth-system, evolution, sustainability and higher-mathematics courses with neuroscience, anatomy, immunity, pharmacology, disease, imaging and machine-learning courses. Each programme therefore contains 82.5 EC not found in the other, above the 30-EC floor.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad life, environmental and quantitative programme is UCR’s strongest integrated response. The Biological-Chemical direction supports a distinct molecular and biomedical second programme. The next direction, biophysics, fails because UCR lacks the necessary physics sequence; the still more physical-chemical and materials direction fails for the same reason plus the absence of chemistry, so production stops at two.

notes.text: Radboud Natural Sciences integrates physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics and, in the selected Physical Chemistry route, continues through quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, chemical bonding, advanced mechanics and electromagnetism. UCR can combine life, environmental and quantitative sciences and can develop a molecular-biological direction, but these are related-fields responses rather than reproductions of the full integrated physical-science curriculum.
